subject.title: [Feature]: Fallback approval mode + model attribution in messages

question: Should OpenClaw add a core opt-in approval gate before executing configured model fallbacks, and if so should the contract be per-agent config, an existing approval/channel event, or a plugin/API extension point?
rationale: The remaining request changes fallback runtime behavior and adds config surface; OpenClaw policy treats fallback behavior and config/default additions as product- and compatibility-sensitive.

options.title: Design Core Opt-In Gate
options.body: Define a default-off per-agent fallback approval contract with timeout behavior, channel delivery semantics, and upgrade-safe schema before implementation.

options.title: Keep Automatic Fallback
options.body: Treat current fallback notices plus response-prefix attribution as the supported visibility/control model and close this direction as not planned after maintainer confirmation.

options.title: Route Through Extension API
options.body: Design a plugin or approval-hook extension point first instead of adding a one-off core model config key.

recommendation.title: Design Core Opt-In Gate
recommendation.body: Define a default-off per-agent fallback approval contract with timeout behavior, channel delivery semantics, and upgrade-safe schema before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest recent history across model-failover docs, config contract work, and the product boundary for fallback behavior.
